uncertainty_budget.explanation: The Indian market price of the token against the official rupee rate for a dollar. This is the bulk of the gap and it is the part everyone argues about.
No rate was published on the settlement date. Stepping back to 2026-06-25 or forward to 2026-06-29 is undetermined — Rule 206 does not say which.
A daily candle is not a price. It is a range with four printed readings and no rule choosing between them.
The retrieved pair is USDT/INR. The receipt was USDC. The figure is USDT/INR x USDC/USDT, and treating the peg as exactly 1.0000 is a further choice.

regimes.outcome: The receipt is classified as income from other sources, recognized on the date of receipt (28 June 2026), valued using the telegraphic transfer buying rate on the last day of the tax year (31 March 2027), and is subject to TDS at 1% if the value exceeds ₹10,000. Disclosed positions are subject to penalties if the explanation is not bona fide or all material facts are not disclosed.

citation.provision: Section 115BBH, Income-tax Act, 1961 — carried into the Income-tax Act, 2025

regimes.reasoning: The receipt of USD 3,000 via bank wire is not a transfer of a virtual digital asset as defined in Section 2(47A). Therefore, it does not fall under Section 115BBH, which specifically taxes income from the transfer of virtual digital assets. Instead, it is classified as income from other sources. The recognition date is the date of receipt (28 June 2026) as per general principles. The valuation method is the telegraphic transfer buying rate on the last day of the tax year (31 March 2027) as per Rule 206(1). The TDS obligation is 1% if the value exceeds ₹10,000, as per Section 393(1) Table Sl. No. 8(vi). Disclosed positions are subject to penalties under Section 439(8) if the explanation is not bona fide or all material facts are not disclosed.
